boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Tom's Brook record (October 9, 1864) in Sheridan's Valley Campaign [August-October 1864]. The October 6-8 harassment of Custer and Merritt and the October 13 reconnaissance at Hupp's Hill are context. Campaign-wide marches, destruction, reinforcements, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen and live force fields read 9,800 total (US 6,300; CS 3,500); the source basis is not given. Early says Rosser had his own brigade and Fitz Lee's two, Lomax two brigades, and that Sheridan concentrated his whole cavalry against them, superior in numbers and equipment. Pond says Merritt and Custer attacked and that Rosser had no conception of Sheridan's mounted strength.
claims.rationale: Brigade lists and an interested judgment of superiority; no counts. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Union victory and the live result Union Victory. Early says Rosser was reportedly falling back in good order while Lomax's command came back in confusion; Pond says the two-hour fight ended in the rout of both, Merritt chasing Lomax twenty miles to Mount Jackson. NPS says the victory gave the Union cavalry overwhelming superiority in the Valley.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The later cavalry superiority is campaign context.

claims.value: The frozen and live casualty fields read 407 total (US 57; CS 350). Early says nine pieces of horse artillery and eight or ten wagons were captured and the loss in men, as he understood, was slight; Pond says eleven guns (five by Merritt, six by Custer), about 330 prisoners and forty-seven wagons were taken, a loss of about 400, against Torbert's 9 killed and 48 wounded.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: Torbert's, Merritt's and Custer's reports, Sheridan's October 9 and 11 dispatches (read, not selected), Rosser's and Lomax's reports and Hotchkiss's journal remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. George E. Pond's The Shenandoah Valley in 1864 (Scribner, 1883) is a retrospective history written, by its preface, from the official documents at the War Records Office and field despatches; it quotes Sheridan's, Torbert's, Wright's and Early's reports and despatches and is not independent of them. Early's reports and dispatches of September 23-October 21, 1864 to Lee are one family of interested Confederate accounts; it is the same author family as his July 14 report selected for Early's Raid. Official Records Series I, Volume XLIII, Part 1 is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
